newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia truckers lift Cartagena strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia truckers lift Cartagena strike.

text.p: BOGOTA, May 6 Reuter - Colombian truck drivers lifted their day-old strike in the Caribbean port of Cartagena Tuesday, partially dispelling fears that the action could spread to the rest of the country, a truckers' leader said.

Regional Labor Ministry representatives agreed to force transport companies to start complying with an agreement signed late last month to increase freight rates and sanction those that did not step into line.

Javier Suarez, head of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association ACC, said his members would be keeping an eye on the situation for the next week but had agreed to end the action which had blocked most goods coming out of Cartagena docks since Monday.

Earlier in the day, Suarez and other ACC leaders threatened the Cartagena strike could spread to the rest of the country if transport companies and freight owners failed to observe the terms of the previous agreement.
The deal, which ended a six-day stoppage by truckers on April 25, included a 30 percent increase in freight rates, a revision of vehicle licensing fees and regulations governing the age of trucks.

The ACC has staged two nationwide strikes in the last six months. The first, an 11-day stoppage, came in October while the second was called in protest at freight companies' failure to comply with the terms of the deal hammered out to end the first strike.
